addresses.comment: COrder slot 34 (+0x88), the 'this order will fight an air-to-air combat' flag. The base returns false and only CAirInterceptOrder and CAirPatrol flip it to the shared `mov al,1` stub; CCarrierProtection computes it: the unit's plain average organisation (`CUnit::GetAverageOrganisation`, slot 20, rva 0x1C6580 - not a share of its maximum) at least **CAG_DUTY_MINIMUM_ORG_LIMIT** (defines `military + 0xEC`), and the order's province (`+0x0C`, which slot 14 keeps at the carrier's) non-null with **an ordinary battle going on in it** - `+0x2F4` is the count of CMapProvince's combat list at +0x2EC. So a carrier's aircraft fight in the air only where a battle is being fought in their carrier's province. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.

addresses.name: CGameState::RemoveUnit
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGameState::RemoveUnit(CGameState* this, CUnit* unit, bool keepOfficers, bool withPassengers)
addresses.revises: The two flags were unestablished. The first, clear, takes the unit's officers off its owner; the second removes what the unit carries with it - an air unit's passengers as well as a fleet's - or lets them go. Parameter names changed from arg2/arg3 to keepOfficers/withPassengers; source moved to the transport findings, which now read it.
addresses.comment:
**A unit ceases to exist**, and this is where it is destroyed.

It unlinks the unit from everything holding it - its country's units, its province, its parent's Children in the order of battle, plans and orders, the interface's selection - takes its regiments off it through RemoveRegimentFromUnit, and then calls **the unit's own scalar deleting destructor**, `unit->vftable->vf_0(1)`. So the object is freed, not handed on.

Its callers are every place a unit is gone for good: a country capitulating or being annexed with units it cannot transfer, CDisbandCommand::Execute, and CUnit::RetreatFromCombat finding nowhere to retreat to.

**The two flags.** With the first clear, the owner's officers fall by the unit's officers times its strength share times the officer ratio, floored at nought. The second decides what becomes of what the unit carries: **a fleet's land units and an air unit's land units alike** are removed with it (RemoveUnit called on each with the same flags) where it is set, and otherwise let go where they stand - a fleet's passengers with +0x300, +0x1C8, +0x2E4 and +0x2E8 cleared, an air unit's with +0x304 and +0x2E8 - with no supplies moved and no battle looked for. Every caller read passes it set but CCountry_Reset and SetGovernmentInExile, so **a transport plane destroyed takes its paratroopers with it**. A land unit removed is taken off its fleet's or its plane's list. A fleet removed also lets go each carrier's air groups - out of the fleet in the order of battle, off the ship's list, a fresh null order, CAir::CheckBase and CUnit::EnterProvince where they stand - before each ship goes to DisposeSubUnit. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, sections A.5, D.1 and D.3.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 2026-10-16. The air branch (from VA 0x6853xx): `if (!IsLand) { if (!IsNaval || navy+0x2ec == 0) { if (IsAir && air+0x2ec != 0) for each node of air+0x2e4: if (arg3) RemoveUnit(this, passenger, arg2, arg3) and the node removed; else the node removed and passenger+0x304, +0x2e8 = 0 } } else the fleet's branch the same with +0x300, +0x1c8, +0x2e4, +0x2e8`. The land side: `+0x300` set -> off the fleet's list; else `+0x304` set -> off the plane's list. The officers: `if (!arg2) officers -= trunc(trunc(strength*1000/max) * officers_of_brigades / 1000) * OfficerRatio / 1000`.
